instructions: Cut the red onion in half and slice it into thin half moons. Put it in a large bowl.
Zest one of the lemons, then squeeze both. That should be about 6 tbsp of juice.
Add 2 tsp of the sumac, 1/2 tsp of the salt and 2 tbsp of the lemon juice to the onion. Rub it all together with your fingers for a minute or two, until the onion goes soft and turns pink.
Drain the 2 cans of beans into a colander and rinse them under cold water. Shake off as much water as you can.
Meanwhile, seed the 3 tomatoes and cut them into small dice. Chop 1 1/2 cups of the parsley leaves.
Add the beans, tomatoes, parsley and the lemon zest to the onion.
In a jar, shake the 1/3 cup oil with the rest of the lemon juice, the last 1 tsp salt and the last 1 tsp sumac until it looks cloudy.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss it gently with a big spoon so the beans stay whole.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lemon.
Warm the 4 pitas in a dry skillet over medium heat, about 30 seconds a side.
Serve with the warm pita, with the Aleppo pepper on the side.
method_notes: All three versions build piyaz from white beans, thinly sliced red onion, tomato and parsley in a sharp olive oil dressing. Dish 'n' the Kitchen (the lead) rubs the onion with sumac, salt and lemon until soft and dresses the canned beans with lemon, sumac and Aleppo pepper; Jamil Ghar adds garlic and lets the beans sit in the dressing for 20 minutes, and Lezzet cooks dried beans and dresses them with grape vinegar. This follows the lead scaled from one large can to two regular cans for a lunch for four, with the Aleppo pepper moved to the side and Jamil Ghar's warm pita alongside.
